title: Grace V. Ringlein
text:
I am a PhD Candidate in Biostatistics at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health (anticipated graduation in May 2027), advised by Elizabeth Stuart and Trang Nguyen. My research focuses on causal inference: determining whether treatments or exposures truly cause changes in outcomes. My dissertation work addresses how to draw causal conclusions from real-world data, such as electronic health records, when key confounders are unobserved or imperfectly measured. I am also interested in measuring disparities and fairness, and in mental health.
For examples of my work, see Demystifying Proximal Causal Inference (methodological) and Income or job loss and psychological distress during the COVID-19 pandemic (applied).
Across my research, teaching, and mentoring, my goal is to make statistical methods accessible to the people who use them, and to support students and collaborators in thinking critically about data-driven evidence.
Click here to read about my experience in the Department of Biostatistics at Johns Hopkins!
